intended_use: Deterministic smoke fixture catalog for evaluation-harness development; not a measured benchmark result.
claim_ceiling: The presence of fixtures is not evidence that Symthaea was evaluated or that any task passed.

cases.prompt: Mira archived the draft report and did not notify anyone.
cases.semantic_contract: Extract actor/action/object and preserve the explicit negative constraint.
cases.claim_ceiling: Fixture defines expected interpretation; it does not establish natural-language competence.

cases.prompt: Remove build artifacts only. Do not delete the source file, lockfile, or any file ending in .keep.
cases.semantic_contract: No excluded path may be treated as an allowed deletion target.
cases.claim_ceiling: Fixture checks constraint preservation only.

cases.prompt: Before committing, run cargo fmt --check and cargo test. If either fails, do not commit or push.

obligations.failure_rule: if either check fails, no commit and no push

cases.semantic_contract: Both checks precede commit; either failure blocks commit and push.
cases.claim_ceiling: Fixture checks the structured plan, not the safety of arbitrary shell execution.

cases.prompt: Change the port in the configuration to 8081.
cases.semantic_contract: Two plausible configuration targets are in context; do not choose one silently.
cases.claim_ceiling: Fixture checks whether ambiguity is exposed, not human preference.

cases.prompt: Return exactly two alternatives. Return only one alternative.

expected.question: Should I return one alternative or two?

cases.semantic_contract: Detect direct contradiction; do not satisfy an arbitrary half.
cases.claim_ceiling: Fixture checks conflict detection for this case.

cases.prompt: Keep the public API unchanged, add a regression test for the defect, and do not add dependencies.
cases.semantic_contract: Canonical obligation set for paraphrase group L-006/L-007.
cases.claim_ceiling: One equivalence pair is a smoke check, not a general paraphrase score.

cases.prompt: Without changing the public API or introducing dependencies, add a regression test that reproduces the bug.
cases.semantic_contract: Canonical obligation set for paraphrase group L-006/L-007; should match L-006.
cases.claim_ceiling: One equivalence pair is a smoke check, not a general paraphrase score.

cases.prompt: Delete the generated report, but preserve the source report.
cases.semantic_contract: The delete and preserve target identities must remain distinct.
cases.claim_ceiling: Fixture checks the declared object distinction only.

cases.prompt: Implement clamp_i32(value, lower, upper) -> i32. Precondition: lower <= upper. Return value clamped to the inclusive [lower, upper] interval.
cases.signature: fn clamp_i32(value: i32, lower: i32, upper: i32) -> i32
cases.test_source: #[test] fn clamp_boundaries() { assert_eq!(clamp_i32(5, 0, 3), 3); assert_eq!(clamp_i32(-2, 0, 3), 0); assert_eq!(clamp_i32(2, 0, 3), 2); assert_eq!(clamp_i32(0, 0, 3), 0); }
cases.claim_ceiling: Passing these tests does not prove all inputs without adequate test/property coverage.

cases.prompt: Implement stable_unique(values: &[i32]) -> Vec<i32>. Keep only the first occurrence of each value, preserving original order.
cases.test_source: #[test] fn stable_unique_order() { assert_eq!(stable_unique(&[3, 1, 3, 2, 1]), vec![3, 1, 2]); assert_eq!(stable_unique(&[]), Vec::<i32>::new()); assert_eq!(stable_unique(&[4, 4]), vec![4]); }
cases.claim_ceiling: Fixture defines a compact behavior contract; it is not a performance benchmark.

cases.prompt: Implement rotate_left<T>(items: &mut [T], amount: usize) -> (). Rotate in place by amount modulo length. Empty input is a no-op.
cases.test_source: #[test] fn rotates() { let mut a = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]; rotate_left(&mut a, 2); assert_eq!(a, [3, 4, 5, 1, 2]); let mut b = [1, 2, 3]; rotate_left(&mut b, 7); assert_eq!(b, [2, 3, 1]); let mut c: [i32; 0] = []; rotate_left(&mut c, 9); assert_eq!(c, []); }
cases.claim_ceiling: Generic-compilation behavior requires running this test under the declared Rust toolchain.

cases.prompt: Implement merge_sorted(left: &[i32], right: &[i32]) -> Vec<i32>. Inputs are ascending; return an ascending merge and preserve all duplicates.
cases.test_source: #[test] fn merge_preserves_duplicates() { assert_eq!(merge_sorted(&[1, 2, 2], &[2, 3]), vec![1, 2, 2, 2, 3]); assert_eq!(merge_sorted(&[], &[1, 2]), vec![1, 2]); assert_eq!(merge_sorted(&[0, 4], &[]), vec![0, 4]); }

properties: all input elements preserved with multiplicity

cases.claim_ceiling: Input sortedness is a precondition, not checked by this function.

cases.prompt: Implement parse_positive_u16(input: &str) -> Option<u16>. Accept only non-empty ASCII decimal digits, with value in 1..=65535. Reject whitespace, a sign, zero, non-ASCII digits and overflow.
cases.test_source: #[test] fn parses_positive_u16() { assert_eq!(parse_positive_u16("1"), Some(1)); assert_eq!(parse_positive_u16("65535"), Some(65535)); assert_eq!(parse_positive_u16("0"), None); assert_eq!(parse_positive_u16("+1"), None); assert_eq!(parse_positive_u16(" 1"), None); assert_eq!(parse_positive_u16("65536"), None); assert_eq!(parse_positive_u16(""), None); }
cases.claim_ceiling: The test source is an initial oracle; additional boundary/property tests are required for promotion.

cases.prompt: Implement first_duplicate(values: &[i32]) -> Option<i32>. Return the value whose second-or-later occurrence appears earliest in the input. Return None if every value is unique.
cases.test_source: #[test] fn first_duplicate_is_by_second_occurrence() { assert_eq!(first_duplicate(&[3, 2, 3, 2]), Some(3)); assert_eq!(first_duplicate(&[1, 2, 3]), None); assert_eq!(first_duplicate(&[]), None); }

properties: first repeat is defined by encounter order, not minimum/maximum duplicate

cases.claim_ceiling: This small fixture is not a general data-structure evaluation.

cases.prompt: Implement checked_sum_range(start: i64, end: i64) -> Option<i64>. Sum the inclusive ascending range using checked arithmetic. If start > end, return Some(0). If the sum overflows i64, return None.
cases.signature: fn checked_sum_range(start: i64, end: i64) -> Option<i64>
cases.test_source: #[test] fn checked_range_sum() { assert_eq!(checked_sum_range(1, 4), Some(10)); assert_eq!(checked_sum_range(4, 3), Some(0)); assert_eq!(checked_sum_range(i64::MAX - 1, i64::MAX), None); assert_eq!(checked_sum_range(0, 0), Some(0)); }
cases.claim_ceiling: Overflow safety must be observed in execution; source inspection alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Implement count_ascii_digits(input: &str) -> usize. Count only ASCII characters '0' through '9'; Unicode numeric characters are not ASCII digits.
cases.claim_ceiling: Fixture checks ASCII classification only, not complete Unicode text handling.

cases.prompt: Repair the implementation so it obeys the clamp_i32 contract. Keep the public signature unchanged.
cases.signature: fn clamp_i32(value: i32, lower: i32, upper: i32) -> i32
cases.buggy_source: fn clamp_i32(value: i32, lower: i32, upper: i32) -> i32 { let _ = lower; value.min(upper) }
cases.repair_contract: Clamp below the lower bound as well as above the upper bound; do not change the signature.
cases.claim_ceiling: One repair fixture does not establish general repair skill.

cases.prompt: Repair stable_unique: remove duplicates without sorting or changing the first-occurrence order.
cases.buggy_source: fn stable_unique(values: &[i32]) -> Vec<i32> { let mut out = values.to_vec(); out.sort(); out.dedup(); out }
cases.repair_contract: Retain first occurrences and original relative order; keep the signature.
cases.claim_ceiling: Passing the supplied case does not prove behavior over all sequences.

cases.prompt: Repair rotate_left so every usize amount is accepted, including amounts larger than the slice length and empty slices.
cases.repair_contract: Normalize the rotation amount; empty input must not panic.
cases.test_source: #[test] fn repaired_rotate() { let mut a = [1, 2, 3]; rotate_left(&mut a, 7); assert_eq!(a, [2, 3, 1]); let mut b: [i32; 0] = []; rotate_left(&mut b, 10); assert_eq!(b, []); }
cases.claim_ceiling: Runtime execution is required to establish no panic on the cases.

cases.prompt: Repair merge_sorted so it preserves multiplicity when values from left and right are equal.
cases.buggy_source: fn merge_sorted(left: &[i32], right: &[i32]) -> Vec<i32> { let (mut i, mut j) = (0, 0); let mut out = Vec::new(); while i < left.len() && j < right.len() { if left[i] < right[j] { out.push(left[i]); i += 1; } else if left[i] > right[j] { out.push(right[j]); j += 1; } else { out.push(left[i]); i += 1; j += 1; } } out.extend_from_slice(&left[i..]); out.extend_from_slice(&right[j..]); out }
cases.repair_contract: Every element from both sorted inputs must appear in the output, including equal values.
cases.claim_ceiling: This fixture detects one specific data-loss defect.

cases.prompt: Repair parse_positive_u16 to reject surrounding whitespace and signs instead of silently normalizing the input.
cases.buggy_source: fn parse_positive_u16(input: &str) -> Option<u16> { let value: u16 = input.trim().parse().ok()?; if value == 0 { None } else { Some(value) } }
cases.repair_contract: Accept only raw ASCII decimal digits representing 1 through 65535.
cases.test_source: #[test] fn repaired_parse() { assert_eq!(parse_positive_u16(" 1"), None); assert_eq!(parse_positive_u16("+1"), None); assert_eq!(parse_positive_u16("1"), Some(1)); }
cases.claim_ceiling: Supplied tests are not a complete parser conformance suite.

cases.prompt: Repair first_duplicate to return the duplicate whose repeated occurrence is encountered first, not the numerically smallest duplicate.
cases.buggy_source: fn first_duplicate(values: &[i32]) -> Option<i32> { let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new(); let mut duplicates = Vec::new(); for &v in values { if !seen.insert(v) { duplicates.push(v); } } duplicates.into_iter().min() }
cases.repair_contract: Return immediately on the first value whose insertion into the seen set fails.

failure_modes: minimum duplicate substituted for first repeated value

cases.claim_ceiling: Fixture tests the stated encounter-order definition only.

cases.prompt: Repair checked_sum_range to report arithmetic overflow as None instead of panicking or wrapping.
cases.signature: fn checked_sum_range(start: i64, end: i64) -> Option<i64>
cases.buggy_source: fn checked_sum_range(start: i64, end: i64) -> Option<i64> { if start > end { return Some(0); } let mut sum = 0_i64; for value in start..=end { sum += value; } Some(sum) }
cases.repair_contract: Use checked arithmetic and return None when the inclusive sum overflows.
cases.test_source: #[test] fn repaired_checked_sum() { assert_eq!(checked_sum_range(i64::MAX - 1, i64::MAX), None); assert_eq!(checked_sum_range(1, 4), Some(10)); }
cases.claim_ceiling: Source inspection is not a substitute for executing overflow controls under the actual build profile.

cases.prompt: Repair count_ascii_digits so it counts ASCII decimal characters only, not every Unicode character classified as numeric.

failure_modes: Unicode numeric classification used instead of ASCII digits

cases.claim_ceiling: This fixture does not establish complete Unicode processing quality.
